rejected.why: make lint already catches it: make lint: UNUSEDSIGNAL

rejected.description: spi_slave takes MOSI straight from its synchroniser, bypassing the MOSI glitch filter, as if only the clock and select lines needed filtering, so data no longer has the same 8-clock delay as the filtered SCK it is sampled against
rejected.why: make lint already catches it: make lint: UNUSEDSIGNAL

rejected.description: The switch-press pulse is qualified by the host enable, as if a host veto had to outrank the physical switch, so a press is ignored exactly when the host has disabled the converter
The rolling-window counts are cross-wired: FCOUNT_RUN (0x15) reports the soft-start window and FCOUNT_SS (0x16) the RUN window

AIM.1.description: Supervisor's latch read-back is wired to the CPLD's own trip drive latch_out instead of the debounced SCR read-back latch_stat_sync_db
AIM.1.reason: When the analog side fires the shared SCR latch (latch_stat high, e.g. OVP) while strike_counter has not asserted latch_out, En stays high and the FSM keeps running instead of going to S_OFF.

AIM.2.description: Supervisor's OTP input takes the synchronised but undebounced OTP flag, bypassing input_debounce
AIM.2.reason: An OTP_trig pulse shorter than the 1 ms assert qualification drops En and forces S_OFF at once, and a real OTP shuts down about 1 ms earlier than the debounced design does.

AIM.3.description: fault_LED's UVLO indication is fed from the undebounced synchronised UVLO flag instead of the debounced copy the supervisor acts on
AIM.3.reason: Red_LED3 lights for UVLO_trig glitches shorter than the debounce time, and follows a real UVLO without the 1 ms / 200 us delay, so the LED disagrees with what the supervisor is acting on.

AIM.4.description: The switch edge detector fires on the falling edge of the debounced switch (release) instead of the rising edge (press)
AIM.4.reason: After the host clears spi_enable over SPI, pressing the switch no longer re-asserts spi_enable, so the converter stays off; spi_enable is re-armed on the switch release instead.

AIM.5.description: switch_supply follows the raw synchronised output comparator instead of the qualified PGOOD from pgood_gen
AIM.5.reason: The housekeeping rail changes over as soon as PGOOD_comp is high, including in S_OFF/S_SS and before the 9 ms in-regulation qualification, so switch_supply and PGOOD differ.

AIM.6.description: fault_LED's power-good input is wired to the synchronised comparator instead of the qualified PGOOD
AIM.6.reason: pgood_LED lights whenever PGOOD_comp is high, even outside S_RUN and during the qualification delay, while PGOOD itself is still low.

AIM.7.description: fault_cause's SCR read-back input is wired to the CPLD's own trip latch_out, so it can no longer tell an external latch from a strike latch
AIM.7.reason: An analog-fired latch (latch_stat high, latch_out low) is never logged as OVP in fault_reg, which the host sees when it reads 0x20.

AIM.8.description: pwm_stats measures the masked PWM_out instead of the synchronised modulator PWM
AIM.8.reason: In S_OFF/S_HICCUP and during soft start pwm_mask truncates each pulse to max_on_counts, so duty_count read over SPI shows the clipped on-time and not the modulator's duty, against its stated purpose.

AIM.9.description: The enable switch debouncer gets the fault-flag asymmetric release time (assert/5, 4 ms) instead of the symmetric 20 ms
AIM.9.reason: Turning the switch off drops En after 4 ms instead of 20 ms, and contact bounce with low gaps between 4 and 20 ms releases the enable and cuts off a running converter.

AIM.10.description: The UVLO debouncer is given the enable's fail-safe-low reset value instead of fault-asserted high, so it disagrees with its high-resetting synchroniser
AIM.10.reason: After reset the debounced UVLO reads healthy instead of faulted: Red_LED3 stays dark for the first 200 us when the pin is low, and with UVLO_trig high it shows the fault only after the 1 ms assert qualification instead of at once.

AIM.11.description: The PWM synchroniser gets the fault inputs' fail-safe-high reset value, as if the PWM were a fault flag
AIM.11.reason: For the first clocks after reset Osc_sync reads high while Osc_in is low, so pwm_mask (pulse_allowed resets to 1) drives a spurious high pulse on PWM_out.

AIM.12.description: The SCK filter is instanced with the fault-flag debounce defaults instead of the short symmetric SPI_FILTER_CLKS
AIM.12.reason: SCK must hold high for 1 ms before the filtered clock rises, so no SCK edge of a 1 MHz transaction reaches spi_slave: writes never take effect and MISO never carries read data.

AIM.13.description: MISO idles high outside the read-data phase (open-drain pull-up convention) instead of held low
AIM.13.reason: MISO is high during the command and CRC phases, between transactions and after reset, where the design specifies it is held low; only during S_READ does it carry the read data.

AIM.14.description: Supervisor's enable input takes the switch-press edge pulse en_switch_rise instead of the debounced switch level
AIM.14.reason: With the switch held on, g_en is high for only the one clock of the press pulse, so the supervisor leaves OFF to S_SS and drops back almost at once. En never stays high and the converter never reaches S_RUN or PGOOD.

AIM.15.description: Switch-press edge detector compares the delayed debounced copy with the synchronised but undebounced switch
AIM.15.reason: en_switch_rise is high for the whole 20 ms debounce interval and on any bounce, even one the debouncer rejects. reg_file then re-asserts spi_enable after a host disable on a bounce that never registers as a press, so the converter can restart.

AIM.16.description: CP_trig goes through the fault-flag input_debounce like OTP and UVLO, though the header says fault_arbiter's rolling window is its only filter
AIM.16.after: logic CP_sync_db; / input_debounce u_CP_sync_db (.clk(clk), .rst_n(rst_n), .flag_in(CP_sync), .flag_out(CP_sync_db)); / fault_arbiter u_fault_arbiter ( .clk(clk), / .rst_n(rst_n), / .trip_run(trip_run), / .trip_ss(trip_ss), / .fault_count_run_out(fault_count_run), / .fault_count_ss_out(fault_count_ss), / .pwm_sync(Osc_sync), / .cp_sync(CP_sync_db),
AIM.16.reason: Valley-current events last part of one switching cycle, far shorter than the debounce assert time, so they never reach fault_arbiter. Repeated overcurrent then never raises window_trip, and the supervisor never goes to S_HICCUP; En stays high.

AIM.17.description: PGOOD_comp is debounced before pgood_gen, so the deassert the header requires to be immediate is delayed by the debounce release time
AIM.17.after: logic PGOOD_comp_sync_db; / input_debounce #(.RESET_VALUE(1'b0)) u_PGOOD_comp_sync_db (.clk(clk), .rst_n(rst_n), .flag_in(PGOOD_comp_sync), .flag_out(PGOOD_comp_sync_db)); / pgood_gen u_pgood_gen ( .clk(clk), / .rst_n(rst_n), / .pwm_sync(Osc_sync), / .pgood_comp(PGOOD_comp_sync_db),
AIM.17.reason: When the output comparator leaves the window during S_RUN, PGOOD and switch_supply stay high for the debounce release time instead of dropping on the next clocks. PGOOD also rises later after the comparator first enters the window.

AIM.18.description: pgood_gen is qualified on the gate-driver enable En instead of run_active, so soft-start counts as running
AIM.18.reason: En is also high in S_SS. If PGOOD_comp is in window during soft-start for the qualify delay, PGOOD and switch_supply assert before SS_done moves the supervisor to S_RUN.

AIM.19.description: strike_counter's clean-run streak is gated on En instead of run_active, so it is not broken by soft-start time
AIM.19.reason: After a hiccup, cycles in S_SS already count toward clean_run_target. strike_level clears earlier than it should, so Red_LED1 stops blinking early and the next hiccup cool-down is shorter.

AIM.20.description: Hiccup back-off is scaled by the configured strike limit max_strikes instead of the current strike_level
AIM.20.reason: Even the first hiccup after a clean history uses the longest back-off. The time En stays low in S_HICCUP before returning to S_SS is longer than the base cool-down.

AIM.21.description: reg_file's status PGOOD bit reports the synchronised output comparator instead of the qualified PGOOD
AIM.21.reason: A host status read during soft-start, in hiccup, or inside the qualify delay shows PGOOD set while the PGOOD pin is low.

AIM.22.description: reg_file's over-temperature status bit takes the undebounced OTP flag, unlike the debounced one the supervisor acts on
AIM.22.reason: A status read during the OTP debounce interval, or after a glitch the debouncer rejects, reports OTP while En is still high and Red_LED2 is off. The header requires telemetry to match what the supervisor acts on.

AIM.23.description: reg_file's latch status bit reports the CPLD's own trip drive latch_out instead of the SCR latch read-back
AIM.23.reason: When the external SCR latch is set by analog protection without a strike trip, En is forced low but a host status read shows no latch.

AIM.24.description: fault_cause's capture gate takes the gate-driver enable En as 'running' instead of the supervisor's run_active, so a hard fault in S_RUN is never logged
AIM.24.reason: En is cleared combinationally by OTP, UVLO, latch_state and latch_assert on the same clock they rise, so when a hard fault stops the converter in S_RUN, convertor_running is already low and the cause bit and fault_time are never captured. An SPI read of the fault register after an OTP or UVLO shutdown from regulation returns 0 for that cause.

AIM.25.description: fault_arbiter's run window is qualified on the gate-driver enable En instead of run_active, so soft-start samples go into the RUN window
AIM.25.reason: En is also high in S_SS, and the run branch comes first. So during soft start every valley sample goes into the 16-cycle RUN window, the SS window never counts, and window_trip_SS never asserts: sustained overcurrent during the ramp no longer sends the supervisor to S_HICCUP, and FCOUNT_SS reads 0 over SPI.

AIM.26.description: OTP debouncer copied from the enable-switch instance above it: symmetric 20 ms qualification instead of the fault-flag default of 1 ms assert and 200 us release
AIM.26.reason: An over-temperature assertion must now last 20 ms instead of 1 ms before En drops and Red_LED2 lights, so an OTP_trig pulse of 1 to 20 ms no longer shuts the converter down. A cleared OTP also takes 20 ms instead of 200 us before the converter may restart.

AIM.27.description: The FAULT_FLAGS register's current-protection bit reports the RUN overcurrent window trip instead of the live synchronised CP comparator
AIM.27.reason: Reading FAULT_FLAGS over SPI while CP_trig is high in S_OFF, S_SS or S_HICCUP, or in S_RUN before the window reaches trip_run, returns the CP bit as 0 instead of 1, unlike the OTP and UVLO bits next to it, which show the live flags.

AIM.28.description: The switch-press edge detector's delayed copy is taken from the undebounced synchronised switch instead of the debounced one it is compared with
AIM.28.reason: The debounced switch rises only after the synchronised level has been high for 20 ms, so the delayed copy is already 1 and en_switch_rise never fires. After the host clears spi_enable, turning the physical switch off and on again no longer re-enables the converter, and En stays low.

AIM.29.description: strike_counter's clean-run streak is gated on the qualified PGOOD instead of run_active, so 'clean running' is taken to mean 'rail in regulation'
AIM.29.reason: The streak cannot start until PGOOD has qualified, about 9 ms into S_RUN, and a dip on PGOOD_comp breaks it while still in S_RUN. Strikes therefore clear later than clean_run_target cycles after reaching S_RUN, or never on a rail that dips. This shows in Red_LED1 blinking longer, in the STRIKE_LEVEL read, and in the next hiccup's back-off and the latch trip.

AIM.30.description: Supervisor's latch_assert input is wired to the debounced SCR read-back instead of strike_counter's own trip latch_out, so the CPLD's strike latch is no longer a hard fault to the FSM
AIM.30.reason: When strike_counter raises latch_out on the MAX_STRIKES-th hiccup entry and the SCR read-back latch_stat does not (yet) follow, the original forces En low and goes to S_OFF; the mutant finishes the cool-down, returns to S_SS and drives En high again.

AIM.31.description: switch_supply is driven from the registered pgood_LED indicator copy instead of PGOOD itself, adding a clock to the changeover hand-back
AIM.31.reason: When PGOOD drops (comparator out of window or leaving S_RUN), switch_supply now deasserts one clock later than PGOOD instead of on the same clock, breaking the immediate hand-back the header requires; assertion is likewise a clock late.

AIM.32.description: pgood_gen is qualified on soft_start's SS_done ('ramp finished') instead of the supervisor's run_active
AIM.32.reason: SS_done is registered in soft_start and only clears a clock after the FSM leaves S_RUN, so on a window trip or hard fault PGOOD and switch_supply drop one clock late instead of immediately; qualification also starts one clock before S_RUN is entered.

AIM.33.description: UVLO debouncer's asymmetry is reversed (fast 200 us assert, slow 1 ms release), the usual 'trip fast, clear slow' rule misapplied where the header wants assert to be the longer qualification
AIM.33.reason: A UVLO_trig pulse lasting between 200 us and 1 ms now shuts the converter down (En low, Red_LED3 on) where it was rejected before, and every UVLO release, including the one after reset, takes 1 ms instead of 200 us before the converter may start.

AIM.34.description: The latch read-back debouncer is given the short symmetric SPI glitch-filter length (8 clocks) instead of the fault-flag 1 ms / 200 us qualification
AIM.34.reason: A latch_stat pulse longer than 160 ns but shorter than 1 ms (switching-node pickup) now forces En low and the FSM to S_OFF, lights Red_LED1 solid, and its release is accepted after 8 clocks instead of 200 us.

AIM.35.description: fault_arbiter's RUN window is enabled by the qualified PGOOD instead of run_active, so overcurrent in S_RUN is only counted while the rail is in regulation
AIM.35.reason: In S_RUN before PGOOD has qualified, or once a short has pulled the rail out of window and dropped PGOOD, the RUN window is held cleared and window_trip never fires, so a sustained CP_trig never sends the converter to hiccup: En stays high where it should go low.

AIM.36.description: reg_file's enable-switch status bit is fed from the gate-driver enable En instead of the debounced switch level
AIM.36.reason: With the switch on but the converter held off (S_OFF on OTP/UVLO, S_HICCUP, or host-disabled), an SPI read of the status register reports the switch as off; it reports on only while the gate driver is actually enabled.

AIM.37.description: soft_start counts its ramp steps on falling edges of the masked PWM_out instead of the synchronised modulator PWM, so each step lands when pwm_mask truncates the pulse rather than after the pulse ends
AIM.37.reason: In S_SS the modulator asks for more on-time than the ceiling, so PWM_out falls in the middle of the Osc pulse. On a step cycle max_on_counts then widens while pwm_mask is parked mid-pulse, which re-opens the envelope, so PWM_out gives a second one-clock pulse in the same switching cycle.

AIM.38.description: fault_cause's latch_assert input is fed from the debounced SCR read-back instead of the CPLD's own trip latch_out, so the OVP inference (latch set with latch_assert clear) can never be true
AIM.38.reason: If the analog OVP comparator trips the shared latch while the converter is in S_SS or S_RUN, the fault-cause register read over SPI shows the LATCH bit instead of the OVP bit, and the OVP bit is never set.

AIM.39.description: strike_counter counts a strike on every entry into soft start (each retry, and the first power-up) instead of on each entry into S_HICCUP
AIM.39.reason: A healthy power-up already gives strike_level 1, so Red_LED1 blinks until the clean-run clear. Under a persistent overcurrent, latch_out asserts on the second retry's entry into S_SS instead of the third hiccup entry, and the hiccup cool-down lengths change.

AIM.40.description: fault_LED's soft-start input is wired to soft_start's SS_done ('ramp finished') instead of the supervisor's ss_active ('in S_SS')
AIM.40.reason: Green_LED stays dark for the whole soft-start ramp of a healthy, unfaulted start-up, and only lights once S_RUN is reached, where the header wants it lit while the converter is switching.

AIM.41.description: fault_cause's episode scope is wired to hiccup_active instead of ss_active, so it counts S_HICCUP as running and leaves S_SS out
AIM.41.reason: An overcurrent that trips window_trip_SS during soft start, or an OTP/UVLO that arrives during S_SS, is never logged in the fault-cause register. A UVLO that arrives during the hiccup cool-down is logged even though the converter was not running.

AIM.42.description: The switch-press detector fires on any change of the debounced switch (press and release) instead of on the press only
AIM.42.reason: If the host disables the converter over SPI and the user then turns the switch off, the release sets spi_enable back to 1, so CONTROL/STATUS read over MISO show the host veto gone without a fresh switch press.

AIM.43.description: The housekeeping changeover drive is gated by the gate-driver enable as well as PGOOD, so it no longer carries the same value as PGOOD
AIM.43.reason: When a hard fault (OTP, UVLO, latch) or a host disable hits in S_RUN with PGOOD high, En drops on the same clock but run_active and PGOOD drop only on the next edge. switch_supply therefore falls one clock before PGOOD, which the header says it should match.

AIM.44.description: soft_start's ramp branch is enabled by the gate-driver enable En instead of ss_active, so the ramp and clamp logic also runs through S_RUN
AIM.44.reason: If the host lowers MAX_ON_LIMIT during S_RUN, max_on_counts is clamped at once and PWM_out on-time is cut under the running loop. The header says the new limit applies only at the next ramp.

AIM.45.description: fault_arbiter's soft-start gate is wired to the gate-driver enable En, so window_trip_SS is not limited to S_SS and can assert in S_RUN from the frozen soft-start count
AIM.45.reason: If TRIP_SS is lowered during S_RUN below the soft-start count held from the ramp, window_trip_SS goes high in S_RUN. fault_cause then logs an overcurrent that never happened, and it shows in the fault-cause register read over SPI.

AIM.46.description: Supervisor's soft-start overcurrent input is wired to the RUN window trip, so the S_SS -> S_HICCUP exit is driven by a trip that fault_arbiter only raises in S_RUN
AIM.46.reason: With CP_trig asserted on enough cycles in S_SS to reach trip_ss, the reference leaves S_SS for S_HICCUP and drops En. The mutant stays in S_SS with En high and PWM_out switching, and never counts a strike.

AIM.47.description: fault_cause's soft-start overcurrent cause is fed from the RUN window trip, so an overcurrent hiccup out of S_SS is not logged
AIM.47.reason: After a window_trip_SS hiccup in S_SS, a host read of the fault-cause register (0x20) gives an OC bit of 0 and a fault_time of 0, where the reference reports OC set and the timestamp of the trip.

AIM.48.description: soft_start holds its ramped ceiling while PGOOD is asserted instead of while the supervisor is in S_RUN, so 'running' is taken to mean 'rail qualified good'
AIM.48.reason: After SS_done the FSM enters S_RUN, but PGOOD is still qualifying, so soft_start falls into its reset branch and drops max_on_counts back to MIN_ON_COUNTS. Until PGOOD asserts, and again after any PGOOD_comp dip, PWM_out pulses are cut to the minimum on-time instead of max_on_limit.

AIM.49.description: fault_cause logs the undebounced synchronised UVLO flag instead of the debounced copy the supervisor acts on
AIM.49.reason: A UVLO_trig pulse in S_SS or S_RUN that is shorter than the debounce assert time does not stop the converter, but the mutant sets the UVLO bit and fault_time in the fault-cause register. The reference logs nothing.

AIM.50.description: strike_counter counts a strike on every gate-driver shutdown (En falling, or low at reset) instead of on each entry into S_HICCUP
AIM.50.reason: Right after reset, and on every switch-off, OTP or UVLO shutdown, strike_level steps up with no hiccup. Red_LED1 blinks, the next hiccup's back-off is longer, and enough plain switch off/on cycles assert latch_out.

AIM.51.description: fault_cause logs the overcurrent cause from the live synchronised CP comparator instead of fault_arbiter's RUN window trip, so a single valley-current excursion counts as an overcurrent fault
AIM.51.reason: In S_SS or S_RUN, a CP_trig pulse too short to reach trip_run sets FAULT_REG bit 0 and latches fault_time. In the original, nothing is logged because the supervisor never left S_RUN.

AIM.52.description: strike_counter breaks its clean-run streak on any CP comparator assertion instead of on the window trip, so 'fault-free' is taken to mean no overcurrent cycle at all
AIM.52.reason: After a hiccup, isolated CP_trig pulses in S_RUN that stay below trip_run keep resetting clean_counter, so strike_level is never cleared. Red_LED1 keeps blinking, the STRIKE_LEVEL read stays non-zero, later cool-downs are longer, and latch_out trips one hiccup sooner than it should.

AIM.53.description: fault_LED's strikes-outstanding input is wired to the configured strike limit max_strikes instead of the accumulated strike_level
AIM.53.reason: With the default non-zero max_strikes and no latch, Red_LED1 blinks from reset onward, even with no hiccup. It also never reflects real strikes when the host has set the limit to 0.

AIM.54.description: fault_LED's running input takes the qualified PGOOD instead of run_active, so the green LED treats 'rail in regulation' as 'running'
AIM.54.reason: From entering S_RUN until pgood_gen finishes PGOOD_DELAY_CYCLES qualifying cycles, and whenever PGOOD_comp dips in S_RUN, Green_LED is dark. In the original it stays lit.

AIM.55.description: fault_LED's soft-start input is wired to hiccup_active, so the green 'running' LED covers the hiccup cool-down instead of soft start
AIM.55.reason: In S_HICCUP with no live hard fault, Green_LED lights although En is low. Through all of S_SS it stays dark, while the original lights it.

AIM.56.description: soft_start's hold branch is keyed on its own SS_done ('ramp finished') instead of S_RUN, so once a ramp completes it is never reset to the floor
AIM.56.reason: After a first ramp and a later hiccup or turn-off, SS_done stays high and max_on_counts stays at max_on_limit. The retry's S_SS goes straight to S_RUN on the next clock, and PWM_out is passed at full ceiling with no re-ramp.

AIM.57.description: Supervisor's enable input takes the synchronised but undebounced switch, bypassing the 20 ms symmetric switch debouncer
AIM.57.reason: En now follows the switch two clocks after it moves instead of 20 ms later, and a bouncing contact starts and abandons a soft-start ramp on every bounce, which shows up as En and PWM activity at the ports.

AIM.58.description: Supervisor's UVLO input takes the synchronised but undebounced UVLO flag, so input-rail sags shorter than the 1 ms assert qualification shut the converter down
AIM.58.reason: A UVLO_trig glitch of a few clocks while running pulls En low at once and sends the FSM to S_OFF, and a UVLO release re-enables after 2 clocks instead of 200 us.

AIM.59.description: Supervisor's SCR latch read-back takes the synchronised but undebounced latch_stat, unlike the debounced copy the header routes to it
AIM.59.reason: A short latch_stat glitch while in S_SS or S_RUN drops En on the same clock and forces S_OFF, though the debounced read-back would have ignored it. After reset the supervisor can also leave S_OFF before the latch read-back has qualified low.

AIM.60.description: fault_arbiter's current flag is wired to the raw CP_trig pin instead of its synchronised copy, while its cycle boundary still comes from the synchronised PWM
AIM.60.reason: The CP history is now two clocks ahead of pwm_rise, so the valley sample comes from BLANK_CLKS+2 clocks before the edge. A CP_trig pulse that ends close to the PWM rising edge is counted or missed differently, which changes when window_trip pulls En low.

AIM.61.description: pwm_mask is fed the raw Osc_in pin instead of the synchronised PWM that every other block uses for the cycle
AIM.61.reason: PWM_out edges move two clocks earlier relative to Osc_in, and the on-time ceiling is measured on a different copy of the PWM than the one soft_start and fault_arbiter count, so PWM_out timing at the port changes on every cycle.

AIM.62.description: reg_file's strike-level status is fed the configured strike limit max_strikes instead of the accumulated strike_level
AIM.62.reason: An SPI read of the strike count returns the limit (3 by default) whether or not any hiccup has happened, and it does not change after a hiccup or a clean-run clear.

AIM.63.description: reg_file's UVLO status bit reports the undebounced synchronised UVLO flag instead of the debounced copy the supervisor acts on
AIM.63.reason: An SPI status read taken during a short UVLO_trig glitch, or within the 1 ms assert qualification, reports undervoltage that the supervisor has not acted on, and it reports release before the debounced flag clears.

AIM.64.description: reg_file's enable-switch status bit is fed the undebounced synchronised switch instead of the debounced level that gates the supervisor
AIM.64.reason: For 20 ms after a switch change, an SPI status read shows the new switch position while the supervisor is still acting on the old one, and contact bounce shows up in the register.

AIM.65.description: fault_cause logs over-temperature from the undebounced synchronised OTP flag instead of the debounced copy the supervisor acts on
AIM.65.reason: An OTP_trig glitch shorter than the 1 ms qualification while running is recorded in fault_reg and timestamped as an over-temperature fault, which the host reads over SPI, even though the converter never shut down for it.

AIM.66.description: fault_LED's over-temperature indication is fed the undebounced synchronised OTP flag instead of the debounced one
AIM.66.reason: Red_LED2 lights on OTP_trig glitches the supervisor ignores. Out of reset it shows the synchroniser's high reset for only two clocks, not until the flag qualifies low, and on release it goes out 200 us earlier than the debounced flag.

AIM.67.description: fault_LED's latch indication takes the CPLD's own trip latch_out instead of the SCR read-back, so an external (OVP) latch trip is not shown
AIM.67.reason: When latch_stat goes high because the analog OVP tripped the SCR, with latch_out still low, Red_LED1 does not go solid. It stays dark or blinks with outstanding strikes.

AIM.68.description: fault_LED's latch_assert input is fed the debounced SCR read-back instead of strike_counter's latch_out, so the CPLD's own strike latch is not shown until the SCR read-back follows
AIM.68.reason: When strike_counter raises latch_out and latch_stat has not yet come back high, Red_LED1 blinks for the outstanding strikes instead of going solid. Green_LED's fault term also misses the strike latch.

AIM.69.description: The CS_n glitch filter is instanced with the fault-flag debounce defaults (1 ms high, 200 us low) instead of the short symmetric SPI_FILTER_CLKS
AIM.69.reason: After CS_n falls, the filtered chip select stays deasserted for 200 us, so every SCK edge of a normal 1 MHz transaction falls outside the frame. Writes never commit and MISO never shows read data.

AIM.70.description: Supervisor's S_RUN overcurrent exit is wired to the soft-start window trip window_trip_SS, so a RUN window trip never sends the FSM from S_RUN to S_HICCUP
AIM.70.reason: fault_arbiter only raises window_trip_SS in S_SS. With this fault, sustained overcurrent on CP_trig in S_RUN leaves En high and the converter in S_RUN with no hiccup, no strike and no latch_out, where the real design drops En and starts a hiccup.

AIM.71.description: Supervisor leaves soft start only when the ramp is done and the output comparator also reports the rail in window, as if 'soft start finished' meant 'output is up'
AIM.71.reason: If PGOOD_comp is low when soft_start raises SS_done, the FSM stays in S_SS instead of moving to S_RUN. PGOOD and switch_supply never assert, and the RUN overcurrent window is never armed, until the comparator goes high.

AIM.72.description: fault_cause's capture gate takes the qualified PGOOD as 'running' instead of run_active, so a fault in S_RUN before PGOOD has qualified, or during a rail dip, is not logged
AIM.72.reason: Say OTP, UVLO or a latch trip shuts the converter down from S_RUN within PGOOD_DELAY_CYCLES of entering it, or while PGOOD_comp is low. The fault-cause register (0x1D) and fault_time then stay empty when the host reads them, where the real design records the cause.

AIM.73.description: reg_file's live TIME registers are fed fault_cause's episode-start snapshot fault_time instead of the free-running timestamp_ms
AIM.73.reason: A host read of TIME_0..TIME_2 (0x18-0x1A) returns zero when no fault is logged, or the frozen episode start time after one, instead of a millisecond count that keeps advancing.

AIM.74.description: fault_cause infers OVP from the synchronised but undebounced SCR read-back instead of the debounced copy the supervisor and LEDs act on
AIM.74.reason: While the converter is in S_SS or S_RUN, a latch_stat pulse shorter than the 1 ms debounce sets the OVP bit and fault_time in the fault-cause register. The supervisor ignores the same pulse and does not shut down.

AIM.75.description: OTP debouncer is given the enable's fail-safe-low reset value, so over-temperature reads clear out of reset while its synchroniser resets high
AIM.75.reason: After reset with OTP_trig low, Red_LED2 and the OTP status bit read low at once, where the real design holds them high for the 200 us release time. If OTP_trig is high at reset, the hot condition is not reported for the first 1 ms.

AIM.76.description: The enable-switch debounce time is converted with ms_to_sw_cycles instead of ms_to_clks, so the debouncer, which counts clk ticks, gets 9000 clocks (180 us) instead of 20 ms
AIM.76.reason: After a switch press, en_from_switch_sync_db, and so En and the start of soft start, follows about 180 us after the switch settles instead of 20 ms. Contact bounce longer than 180 us now passes through as separate presses and releases, which toggles En and restarts the ramp.

AIM.77.description: reg_file's SCR latch status bit takes the synchronised but undebounced latch_stat instead of the debounced copy the supervisor acts on
AIM.77.reason: If latch_stat glitches high for less than the 1 ms assert qualification, a host read of the status register shows the latch as set even though the supervisor never saw it. A real latch release also shows up 200 us before the supervisor acts on it, so telemetry no longer matches what the supervisor is acting on.

AIM.78.description: reg_file's enable-switch status bit is fed the switch-press edge pulse en_switch_rise instead of the debounced switch level
AIM.78.reason: While the switch is held on, a host read of the status register shows the enable switch as off. It reads as on only during the single clock after a debounced press.

AIM.79.description: fault_LED's latch indication is fed the synchronised but undebounced SCR read-back instead of the debounced copy
AIM.79.reason: A latch_stat pulse shorter than the 1 ms assert qualification lights Red_LED1 solid even though the supervisor ignores it. A real latch also shows on Red_LED1 up to 1 ms before the supervisor shuts down.

AIM.80.description: The latch read-back debouncer is given the enable's fail-safe-low reset value, so the SCR latch reads clear out of reset although its synchroniser resets high
AIM.80.reason: If the SCR is still latched when reset is released, Red_LED1 and the latch status bit stay off for the first 1 ms instead of showing the latch at once. If the pin is low, the 200 us of latched indication that follows reset is missing.

AIM.81.description: The OTP debouncer's asymmetry is reversed: 200 us to assert and 1 ms to release, the 'trip fast, clear slow' habit applied where the design wants assert to be the longer qualification
AIM.81.reason: An OTP_trig pulse between 200 us and 1 ms long now shuts the converter down (En falls, Red_LED2 lights), when it should be rejected. Recovery after over-temperature clears is also delayed from 200 us to 1 ms.

AIM.82.description: The MOSI glitch filter is instanced with the fault-flag debounce times (1 ms high, 200 us low) instead of the short symmetric SPI_FILTER_CLKS, so it no longer matches the SCK filter
AIM.82.reason: At 1 MHz SCK no MOSI bit is held for 1 ms, so every bit spi_slave shifts in reads as 0. Every command fails its CRC: host writes to CONTROL and the limit registers are discarded, and reads return the wrong register or nothing.

AIM.83.description: The UVLO debouncer is copied from the enable-switch instance above it, so it gets the symmetric 20 ms switch qualification instead of the fault-flag default of 1 ms assert and 200 us release
AIM.83.reason: An input-rail sag on UVLO_trig lasting between 1 ms and 20 ms no longer drops En or lights Red_LED3. After a real UVLO, the converter also waits 20 ms instead of 200 us before it can restart and Red_LED3 goes out.

AIM.84.description: The SCR latch read-back debouncer has its asymmetry reversed: it asserts after 200 us and releases after 1 ms, the 'trip fast, clear slow' habit applied where the fault flags want assert to be the longer qualification
AIM.84.reason: A latch_stat pulse that lasts between 200 us and 1 ms now counts as a latched trip. It drops En, sends the FSM to S_OFF and lights Red_LED1 solid, where the original filters it out. Once latch_stat goes low, the trip also stays asserted 1 ms instead of 200 us.

AIM.85.description: MISO is enabled whenever the slave is selected (CS_n low), the usual 4-wire convention, instead of only during the read-data phase (S_READ)
AIM.85.reason: While CS_n is low, MISO now shows whatever sdio_out holds outside the read phase. That is the last bit of the previous read during the next command byte, and rdata[7] already in the second half of the turnaround byte. The original holds MISO low through both.

AIM.86.description: strike_counter counts a strike when the hiccup cool-down finishes (hiccup_done) instead of when S_HICCUP is entered
AIM.86.reason: Each strike now lands at the end of its cool-down. hiccup_timer therefore times every cool-down at the previous strike level: 5 ms instead of 10 ms for the first hiccup, 10 ms instead of 20 ms for the second, so En comes back early. latch_out also asserts at the end of the third cool-down instead of on entry to it, and a hiccup cut short by a hard fault counts no strike at all.

AIM.87.description: The SCR latch read-back debouncer is copied from the enable-switch instance, so it gets the symmetric 20 ms switch qualification instead of the fault-flag default of 1 ms assert and 200 us release
AIM.87.reason: Suppose the analog OVP sets the SCR latch, so latch_stat goes high while latch_out stays low. The supervisor, Red_LED1 and the STATUS latch bit now see it only after 20 ms instead of 1 ms, so En stays high and the FSM stays in S_SS/S_RUN for about 19 ms longer. A cleared latch also takes 20 ms instead of 200 us to release.

AIM.88.description: The OTP debouncer is copied from the SPI glitch filters, so over-temperature is qualified in 8 clocks (160 ns) both ways instead of the fault-flag 1 ms assert and 200 us release
AIM.88.reason: An OTP_trig pulse longer than 8 clocks but shorter than 1 ms now drives the supervisor to S_OFF and pulls En low, and it lights Red_LED2. The correct design ignores such a pulse. After a real over-temperature, OTP also clears 160 ns after the comparator drops instead of 200 us later.

AIM.89.description: fault_arbiter's valley-sample cycle boundary is taken from the masked, registered gate PWM_out instead of the synchronised modulator PWM, so each per-cycle CP sample lands one clock after the modulator's turn-on edge
AIM.89.reason: pwm_mask registers its output, so PWM_out rises one clock after Osc_sync. The BLANK_CLKS lookback then reads the CP comparator 4 clocks before the modulator edge instead of 5. A CP_trig excursion that sits only in that one-clock band is now counted, or now missed, so the fault counts and the window_trip/window_trip_SS hiccup exits (seen on En) change for the same CP_trig/Osc_in stimulus.

AIM.90.description: pgood_gen counts its qualifying switching cycles on falling edges of the masked gate PWM_out instead of the synchronised modulator PWM
AIM.90.reason: In S_RUN with the comparator good, the qualify counter now steps on PWM_out falling edges. These lag Osc_sync by one clock when the pulse is not truncated and come earlier when pwm_mask cuts it at the ceiling. So PGOOD and switch_supply assert on a different clock from the one the modulator cycle count gives.

AIM.91.description: fault_cause's 'converter running' scope takes soft_start's SS_done ('ramp finished') instead of the supervisor's ss_active ('in S_SS'), so faults during the ramp are outside the episode
AIM.91.reason: While in S_SS before the ramp completes, SS_done is low. A window_trip_SS hiccup, or OTP/UVLO/latch faults that end soft start, therefore set no FAULT_CAUSE bit and no fault_time, and a later SPI read of the fault log returns zero. The same faults in S_RUN are still logged.

AIM.92.description: spi_slave is handed the inverted filtered SCK, as if the bus were CPOL=1 (Mode 3) instead of Mode 0, so it samples MOSI on the master's falling SCK edge and shifts MISO on the rising edge
AIM.92.reason: In every SPI transaction the slave samples and shifts on the wrong clock phase, and it sees SCK idling high. Command, address, write data and CRC are taken half a bit late, so register writes are rejected or land wrongly and MISO read data is shifted, which shows on the MISO pin and in the control outputs.

AIM.93.description: pwm_stats measures the inverted modulator PWM, so DUTY_COUNT reports the low-side (off) time of each cycle instead of the high-side on-time
AIM.93.reason: Once the modulator is switching, a host read of DUTY_COUNT (0x13) returns about period minus on-time instead of the on-time, for any duty other than 50%. PREV_PERIOD is now measured falling edge to falling edge, so it still reads about the same in steady state.

AIM.94.description: fault_arbiter's per-cycle CP sample is taken at high-side turn-off (the falling PWM edge, near peak current) instead of at turn-on (the valley), mixing up which edge ends low-side conduction
AIM.94.reason: In S_SS and S_RUN each window sample, and so each window_trip / window_trip_SS, is taken one on-time away from the valley instant. A CP_trig level that is present at one edge but not the other is counted wrongly, so the time En drops and the FSM enters hiccup moves, and FCOUNT_RUN/FCOUNT_SS read differently.

AIM.95.description: soft_start counts ramp cycles and widens the ceiling at the PWM turn-on edge instead of after each pulse has ended, so each step lands as a pulse starts
AIM.95.reason: During S_SS each ceiling step lands at the rising edge of the cycle that completes the step count, so that pulse already gets the wider ceiling. The masked PWM_out pulses widen one cycle earlier than the design intends, and SS_done (so the move to S_RUN) comes one on-time early.

AIM.96.description: strike_counter takes its clean-run cycle boundary from the masked, registered gate PWM_out instead of the synchronised modulator PWM
AIM.96.reason: In S_RUN after a hiccup, the clean-run counter now steps when PWM_out falls: one clock late, or early at the on-time ceiling when the pulse is truncated. So the strike_level clear, and the moment Red_LED1 stops blinking, moves off the modulator's cycle boundary that the rest of the design uses.

AIM.97.description: soft_start's hold branch covers S_HICCUP as well as S_RUN, so a hiccup does not reset the ramped ceiling and SS_done to the floor; only S_OFF does
AIM.97.reason: After a RUN overcurrent sends the FSM into S_HICCUP, the retry enters S_SS still holding SS_done=1 and the full max_on_limit ceiling. The supervisor moves to S_RUN one clock later and PWM_out runs at full on-time without re-ramping, which the header requires every hiccup retry to do.

AIM.98.description: spi_enable, the host's CONTROL run-enable for the converter, is mistaken for an SPI-interface enable and gates the slave's chip select, so a host that disables the converter is locked off the bus
AIM.98.reason: After the host writes CONTROL to clear spi_enable, every later SPI transaction is ignored: writes are not applied and MISO stays low on reads. This lasts until a switch press re-asserts spi_enable. In the correct design the bus keeps working while the converter is host-disabled.

AIM.99.description: spi_slave is handed the inverted filtered chip select, as if CS were active high, so the idle bus looks selected and a real transaction looks deselected
AIM.99.reason: While the master holds CS_n low for a transaction, the slave sees itself deselected, so it shifts in no command, applies no write and never drives read data on MISO. Its framing instead runs while CS_n idles high.

AIM.100.description: pwm_mask's PWM input is gated by the gate-driver enable En, adding the second logic shutdown path that the header explicitly rules out
AIM.100.reason: In S_OFF and S_HICCUP, or whenever a fault pulls En low, PWM_out stays low instead of carrying the masked modulator pulses. A fault that drops En mid-pulse also cuts the PWM_out pulse short on that same clock.

AIM.101.description: hiccup_timer is given strike_level minus one, as if the strike count had not already been incremented on entry to S_HICCUP, so each cool-down is half its intended length
AIM.101.reason: The first hiccup re-enables En after one base interval (5 ms by default) instead of two (10 ms), and the second after 10 ms instead of 20 ms. The time S_HICCUP holds the gate driver off before each retry is halved.

AIM.102.description: pgood_gen's qualifying delay is converted with ms_to_clks, as for the debouncers, although pgood_gen counts switching cycles, so the 9 ms qualification becomes 450000 PWM cycles (about 1 s)
AIM.102.reason: After the supervisor enters S_RUN with the output comparator good, PGOOD and switch_supply assert about 1 s later instead of about 9 ms later. pgood_LED is delayed by the same amount.

AIM.103.description: In S_RUN, pwm_mask takes its on-time ceiling straight from the host's max_on_limit register instead of the ceiling soft_start ramped to and now holds
AIM.103.reason: If the host writes a new MAX_ON_LIMIT while the converter is in S_RUN, PWM_out pulses are cut to the new limit at once. The header says the held ceiling stays until the next ramp. When a lowered limit sits between the old ceiling and the modulator's pulse width, the PWM_out pulse width changes during S_RUN.

AIM.104.description: The FAULT_FLAGS current-protection status bit is masked by the gate-driver enable, on the idea that the valley comparator only means something while the stage is switching
AIM.104.reason: While the converter is in S_OFF or S_HICCUP, or out of reset with CP_trig high (it resets high, fail-safe), an SPI read of FAULT_FLAGS returns the CP bit as 0 instead of the live synchronised comparator level.

AIM.105.description: The CPLD's own strike trip latch_out is ORed into the SCR read-back before debouncing, as if the read-back had to follow the CPLD's drive, so the latch read-back no longer reports only the physical SCR
AIM.105.reason: After strike_counter asserts latch_out, the latch status bit in reg_file reads set 1 ms later even if the latch_stat pin stays low. Until reset, the debounced latch_state also stays set whatever the pin does.

AIM.106.description: hiccup_timer is handed strike_level plus one, as if it had to anticipate strike_counter's increment on entry to S_HICCUP, so every cool-down is one doubling longer than the strike count calls for
AIM.106.reason: strike_counter has already incremented by the time the cool-down runs, so the first hiccup lasts base<<2 (20 ms by default) instead of base<<1 (10 ms), and at strike level 3 the 2-bit sum wraps to the base interval. The time En is held low in S_HICCUP before the retry into S_SS changes on every hiccup.

AIM.107.description: MISO is tri-stated outside the read-data phase, following the usual shared-bus SPI slave habit, instead of being driven low as a plain output
AIM.107.reason: At every time except spi_slave's S_READ phase (idle, command, address and write phases), MISO floats at Z instead of reading 0. That breaks the header's rule that MISO is a plain output with no tri-state anywhere in the design.

AIM.108.description: pwm_stats measures the synchronised modulator PWM only while the gate driver is enabled, though its block comment says it runs unconditionally because duty and period matter as much during a fault
AIM.108.reason: In S_OFF and S_HICCUP, or while a hard fault pulls En low, the modulator still toggles Osc_in, but pwm_stats sees a flat line. Its period counter saturates and DUTY_COUNT and PERIOD stop following the modulator, so SPI reads of those registers return stale or all-ones values.

AIM.109.description: The housekeeping changeover drive is held on for one extra clock after PGOOD drops, ORed with the registered pgood_LED copy as a glitch hold-off, so the hand-back is no longer immediate
AIM.109.reason: switch_supply still rises with PGOOD, but when PGOOD deasserts (the rail leaves its window, or the converter leaves S_RUN) switch_supply stays high one clock longer. At that moment it differs from PGOOD, against the header's rule that it carries the same value with no added delay.

AIM.110.description: fault_arbiter's current flag is qualified by the modulator PWM, as if the current comparator were only valid during high-side on-time, though it is a valley comparator sampled in low-side conduction
AIM.110.reason: fault_arbiter's sample at pwm_rise reads the comparator from BLANK_CLKS clocks before turn-on, when PWM is low. So every sample is 0, and a sustained CP_trig in S_SS or S_RUN never trips a window or sends the converter into hiccup.

AIM.111.description: fault_cause's 'converter running' capture scope also covers S_HICCUP, as if the hiccup cool-down were part of the operating episode
AIM.111.reason: latch_assert rises one clock after S_HICCUP is entered on the final strike, and OTP/UVLO can assert during the cool-down. With this edit those are logged in FAULT_CAUSE (BIT_LATCH, BIT_OTP, BIT_UVLO) with a fault_time, where the design leaves them out because the converter is stopped.

AIM.112.description: reg_file's enable-switch status bit reports the combined enable (switch AND host CONTROL enable) instead of the physical switch alone
AIM.112.reason: After the host disables the converter over SPI (keyed disable) with the switch still on, STATUS bit 4 reads 0 instead of 1. The host can then no longer tell its own veto from the switch being off.

AIM.113.description: reg_file's SCR latch status bit shows only externally-originated latch trips, masking the read-back whenever the CPLD's own latch_out is driving, as if it were fault_cause's OVP inference
AIM.113.reason: After a strike latch (latch_out high) with the SCR read back set, STATUS bit 3 reads 0 instead of 1. It only reports the latch when it is tripped by the analog side.

AIM.114.description: The CPLD's trip drive latch_out is released once the debounced SCR read-back shows the latch set, as if the self-holding SCR needed the drive only until it fired, instead of following strike_counter's set-only latch_assert
AIM.114.after: logic strike_latch; / strike_counter u_strike_counter ( .clk(clk), / .rst_n(rst_n), / .max_strikes(max_strikes), / .clean_run_target(clean_run_target), / .pwm_sync(Osc_sync), / .hiccup_active(hiccup_active), / .run_active(run_active), / .window_trip(window_trip), / .strike_level(strike_level), / .latch_assert(strike_latch) / ); / assign latch_out = strike_latch & ~latch_stat_sync_db;
AIM.114.reason: After a strike latch, latch_out at the port drops about 1 ms after latch_stat reads back high, where it should stay high until reset. Every consumer of latch_assert (supervisor, fault_cause, fault_LED) then sees it clear while the SCR stays set, so the strike latch looks like an external one.

AIM.115.description: fault_cause's clear-on-read also fires on spi_abort, as if any transaction that ended unvalidated also closed the fault-log read window, so a failed write wipes the fault record and its start time
AIM.115.reason: Suppose fault causes have been logged and the host then sends a write that is aborted (bad CRC, wrong length or timeout). A later SPI read of FAULT_CAUSE and FTIME returns zero instead of the logged causes and episode-start timestamp.

AIM.116.description: reg_file's read snapshot of the timestamp is retaken after every read data byte clocked out instead of only on the first data byte of the read
AIM.116.reason: In a burst read of TIME_0..TIME_2, the bytes come from different instants. If a millisecond tick (in particular a carry from byte 0 into byte 1 or 2) lands mid-transaction, the host gets a torn timestamp. The design should return one coherent value frozen at the start of the transaction.

AIM.117.description: Chip-select deassert is taken straight from the unfiltered synchronised CS_n, so only selection goes through the glitch filter, as if 'deselect must be immediate'
AIM.117.reason: A CS_n glitch high shorter than the 8-clock filter in the middle of a transaction now reaches spi_slave as a cs_rise and aborts it. CS also now rises 8 clocks ahead of the filtered SCK and MOSI, so a master that raises CS within 160 ns of its last SCK edge has its final CRC bit cut off and the write is discarded.

AIM.118.description: strike_counter is handed the strike limit minus one, a second off-by-one fix on top of the one strike_counter already makes by comparing with max_strikes-1
AIM.118.reason: With the default limit of 3, latch_out (and so the shared SCR latch, Red_LED1 and the S_OFF lockout) trips on the 2nd hiccup entry instead of the 3rd. The two-retries-then-latch sequence becomes one retry.

AIM.119.description: The UVLO debouncer is copied from the SPI glitch filters, so input undervoltage qualifies in 8 clocks (160 ns) both ways instead of the fault-flag 1 ms assert and 200 us release
AIM.119.reason: An input-rail sag or changeover transient longer than 160 ns but shorter than 1 ms now asserts UVLO. That drops En, sends the supervisor to S_OFF and lights Red_LED3 on a healthy board. A real UVLO also releases after 160 ns instead of 200 us, so the converter restarts sooner.

AIM.120.description: reg_file's write strobe is qualified by spi_integrity_ok, as if only validated bytes should reach the register file, though reg_file stages every data byte and validates later at commit
AIM.120.reason: integrity_ok pulses only at cs_rise, at least one clock after the last wr_en, so the two never coincide and no write reaches reg_file: SCRATCH, CONTROL disable/enable and every threshold write are lost and read back unchanged after a write with a valid CRC.

AIM.121.description: reg_file commits staged writes at the end of any write transaction (integrity_ok or txn_abort), mixing up 'transaction ended' with 'transaction validated'
AIM.121.reason: A write frame with a bad CRC or a misaligned CS rise now commits its SCRATCH, CONTROL or threshold bytes. A read-back after a corrupted write shows the new value instead of the old one, and a corrupted armed CONTROL disable stops the converter.

AIM.122.description: reg_file's txn_abort is driven on every write-transaction end, valid or not, as if it only meant 'discard the temporaries now', so the bus-error tally also counts good transactions
AIM.122.reason: Commits still happen, but BUS_ERR_L/H goes up by one for every valid write too. After a clean write sequence the host reads a non-zero bus-error count where it should read zero.

AIM.123.description: fault_cause's clear-on-read is also required to come from a CRC-validated transaction, as if the destructive clear needed write-style validation, though reads never produce integrity_ok
AIM.123.reason: fault_reg_read_done fires during a read and integrity_ok only at the end of a write, so FAULT_CAUSE and FTIME are never cleared by the host's read of 0x20. A second read after the fault has gone still returns the old cause and start time.

AIM.124.description: fault_cause's record is cleared when any read transaction starts (rd_first) as well as after 0x20 is read, taking 'clear on read' to mean 'clear when a read begins'
AIM.124.reason: Polling any register, for example STATUS, wipes a logged fault before the host reads it. A sweep starting at 0x1D gets the cause byte but reads FTIME 0x1E-0x20 as zero, because fault_time is cleared on the clock after the first byte loads.

AIM.125.description: reg_file's 'data byte transferred' strobe also counts write data bytes, so a write that releases a byte at 0x20 counts as the host having read the fault record
AIM.125.reason: A host write burst that reaches the read-only address 0x20 clears FAULT_CAUSE and FTIME with nothing read. reg_file's own comment says a write releasing a byte must not clear the record, and a later read of 0x1D returns 0 although a fault was logged.

AIM.126.description: soft_start's ramp floor is set from the wanted gate on-time MIN_GATE_ON_NS alone, without the LM5106 turn-on shrinkage, so the floor is 6 clocks instead of 12
AIM.126.reason: Whenever the supervisor enters S_SS (first start or a hiccup retry), the first PWM_out pulses are cut off after 6 clocks instead of 12. The ramp then has more steps to climb, so SS_done and the move to S_RUN come later.

AIM.127.description: soft_start is handed cycles_per_step minus one, an off-by-one fix applied a second time on top of soft_start's own compare against cycles_per_step-1
AIM.127.reason: In S_SS the ceiling on PWM_out pulses widens every 15 switching cycles instead of 16 with the default register, so SS_done and the move to S_RUN come early. If the host writes cycles_per_step = 1, the ramp never steps and the FSM stays in soft start.

AIM.128.description: spi_slave's SCK rising edge is taken straight from the unfiltered synchronised SCK, so only the falling edge goes through the glitch filter, as if the filter were needed only on release
AIM.128.reason: A high glitch on SCK shorter than SPI_FILTER_CLKS, arriving while CS_n is low, now reaches spi_slave as an extra rising edge and clocks in an extra bit. The write then fails its CRC or the read returns shifted data, where the filtered design ignores the glitch.

AIM.129.description: spi_slave's 2 ms dead-master SCK idle timeout is converted with ms_to_sw_cycles instead of ms_to_clks, so the slave, which counts clk ticks, times out after 900 clocks (18 us)
AIM.129.reason: A transaction where CS_n stays low and SCK pauses for more than 18 us but less than 2 ms (for example a gap between bytes) is aborted. A write in that situation is discarded and a read stops driving MISO, where the 2 ms timeout would let both complete.

AIM.130.description: pgood_gen's qualifying count is set to 2**PGOOD_DELAY_W, following the package's out-of-date note that the counter saturates at all-ones, instead of PGOOD_DELAY_CYCLES
AIM.130.reason: In S_RUN with the output rail good, PGOOD and switch_supply assert 4096 switching cycles after qualifying starts instead of 4050, about 100 us later than the 9 ms the design calls for.

AIM.131.description: The 20 ms enable debouncer is fed the combined enable (switch AND host CONTROL enable) instead of the physical switch alone, as if 'the enable' to be debounced were the supervisor's g_en
AIM.131.reason: A host CONTROL disable now takes 20 ms to drop En instead of acting on the commit clock. Once the host has disabled the converter, the debounced switch stays low whatever the switch does, so a fresh switch press never makes en_switch_rise and cannot re-assert spi_enable. Only another host enable or the watchdog brings the converter back.

AIM.132.description: hiccup_timer is kept armed through the soft-start retry as well as S_HICCUP, as if cool-down plus re-ramp were one episode, so hiccup_done is not cleared on leaving S_HICCUP for S_SS
AIM.132.reason: After a cool-down ends and the FSM retries in S_SS, hiccup_done stays high. If that soft start then trips window_trip_SS, the FSM leaves the next S_HICCUP on the next clock and En comes back almost at once instead of after the doubled cool-down. On first power-up the timer also runs during S_SS, so a soft-start trip more than 5 ms after start-up skips its cool-down.

AIM.133.description: fault_cause's over-temperature input is qualified by the gate-driver enable, meant as 'only faults that interrupted switching', but the supervisor drops En combinationally on OTP itself
AIM.133.reason: En is already forced low on the same clock that the debounced OTP asserts, so fault_cause never sees OTP while the converter is in S_SS or S_RUN. An over-temperature shutdown then leaves the OTP bit of the 0x20 fault record clear, and no episode start time is captured for it.

AIM.134.description: The fault-log timebase prescaler is set with ms_to_sw_cycles(1) instead of the clk-based package value. The timestamp counts clk ticks, so a 'millisecond' tick comes every 450 clocks (9 us) instead of every 50000.
AIM.134.reason: timestamp_ms advances about 111 times too fast. So the TIME_0..2 registers (0x18-0x1A) and the FTIME episode-start bytes (0x1E-0x20) read over SPI report elapsed time far larger than the real milliseconds since reset or since the fault.

AIM.135.description: The Red_LED1 strike blink half-period is sized in switching cycles (ms_to_sw_cycles(125)), to match the clean-run window it was chosen against. But fault_LED's blink counter counts clk ticks, so it gets 56250 clocks (about 1.1 ms) instead of 125 ms.
AIM.135.reason: While strikes are outstanding (strike_level non-zero, no latch), Red_LED1 toggles about every 1.1 ms instead of every 125 ms, so the 4 Hz strike blink at the port becomes roughly 440 Hz.

AIM.136.description: The per-strike doubling of the hiccup cool-down is also applied at the call site, so hiccup_timer gets a base already shifted by strike_level and shifts it again: each strike quadruples the interval instead of doubling it.
AIM.136.reason: With the default 5 ms base, the S_HICCUP off-time (En held low) is 20 ms instead of 10 ms after the first strike, and 80 ms instead of 20 ms after the second, before the FSM retries soft start.

AIM.137.description: The slave is selected straight from the unfiltered synchronised CS_n and only the deselect goes through the glitch filter, as if 'selection must be immediate'.
AIM.137.reason: A low CS_n blip shorter than the 8-clock filter now reaches spi_slave as a cs_fall and cs_rise with no complete command byte. That counts as an aborted write, so txn_abort pulses and reg_file's bus-error tally goes up where the filtered design would have seen nothing; the host sees it when it reads the tally back over MISO.

AIM.138.description: MISO is also cut by the unfiltered synchronised CS_n, so read data drops at once on a deselect (or a CS glitch) instead of following spi_slave's S_READ phase on the filtered chip select
AIM.138.reason: During a read, MISO goes low about SPI_FILTER_CLKS clocks before sdio_oe falls after CS_n rises. A CS_n glitch shorter than the filter, which spi_slave ignores, now forces MISO low in the middle of a read data bit.

AIM.139.description: reg_file's STATUS power-good bit is fed fault_LED's registered pgood_LED copy instead of PGOOD itself, so telemetry lags the changeover by a clock
AIM.139.reason: A STATUS read whose snapshot falls on the clock where PGOOD changes (PGOOD qualifies, or drops on a rail dip or on leaving S_RUN) returns the old PGOOD value. That disagrees with the PGOOD and switch_supply pins.

AIM.140.description: reg_file's SCR latch status bit ORs in the CPLD's own trip drive latch_out, as if 'latch set' meant 'either source driving it', instead of reporting the debounced physical read-back alone
AIM.140.reason: After a strike latch, the latch status bit reads 1 as soon as latch_out asserts, before the SCR read-back has debounced. It stays 1 even if the SCR never fires, so STATUS no longer shows only the read-back the supervisor acts on.

AIM.141.description: pgood_gen's 'regulating' qualifier is also ANDed with the gate-driver enable, as if PGOOD had to drop with the combinational fault gating of En rather than when the supervisor leaves S_RUN
AIM.141.reason: When OTP, UVLO or a latch trip asserts in S_RUN, PGOOD and switch_supply now fall on the same clock as En instead of one clock later, when run_active falls. The qualify counter is also cleared one clock earlier.

AIM.142.description: strike_counter is handed the clean-run target minus one, taking the counter to count from zero to target-1, although it clears strikes when clean_counter equals the target itself
AIM.142.reason: After a hiccup and a retry into S_RUN, strike_level (and the Red_LED1 strike blink) clears after clean_run_target-1 fault-free switching cycles instead of clean_run_target. The strike level is visible over SPI and on Red_LED1.

AIM.143.description: fault_cause's episode-start snapshot is wired to its own fault_time output instead of the free-running timestamp_ms, a slip between the two adjacent TIMESTAMP_W ports, so the snapshot just reloads the cleared value
AIM.143.reason: After a fault episode in S_SS or S_RUN, the host reads the FAULT_TIME bytes over SPI and gets 0 instead of the timestamp at which the episode began. The live TIME registers stay correct because reg_file still takes timestamp_ms.

AIM.144.description: Supervisor's S_RUN overcurrent exit takes the live synchronised CP comparator instead of fault_arbiter's RUN window trip, so the rolling-window duration filter is bypassed for the FSM
AIM.144.reason: In S_RUN, any CP_trig assertion that reaches CP_sync, even a single cycle well below trip_run faulted cycles, moves the FSM to S_HICCUP on the next edge. En drops and a strike is counted where the original keeps running until the window count reaches trip_run.

AIM.145.description: Supervisor's soft-start overcurrent exit takes the live synchronised CP comparator instead of fault_arbiter's soft-start window trip, so the higher soft-start tolerance trip_ss is never applied
AIM.145.reason: In S_SS, the first CP_trig excursion, which is expected while the output capacitor charges, sends the FSM to S_HICCUP. En drops and the ramp aborts, where the original only does so once trip_ss faulted cycles have been seen in the window.

AIM.146.description: The valley-current comparator is taken as active low (open-drain fault convention) at fault_arbiter, so a low CP_trig counts as an overcurrent cycle
AIM.146.reason: With CP_trig low (no overcurrent), every switching cycle in S_SS is sampled as faulted, so window_trip_SS fires after trip_ss cycles and the converter hiccups on every start. A real sustained overcurrent (CP_trig high) never trips either window.

AIM.147.description: The UVLO comparator is read as an 'input good' signal (high when the input rail is above threshold), so its synchronised level is inverted before debouncing
AIM.147.reason: With a healthy input (UVLO_trig low), UVLO_sync_db stays asserted. The supervisor never leaves S_OFF, En stays low and Red_LED3 stays lit. An actual undervoltage (UVLO_trig high) releases the flag and lets the converter start.

AIM.148.description: The SCR latch read-back is taken as active low (the anode node pulled down when the SCR fires), so the synchronised read-back is inverted before debouncing
AIM.148.reason: With the latch not tripped (latch_stat low), latch_stat_sync_db stays set. The supervisor stays in S_OFF, Red_LED1 is solid and the STATUS latch bit reads set. A real latch trip (latch_stat high) clears it and lets the converter run.

AIM.149.description: The over-temperature comparator is read as active low (the open-drain thermal-warning convention), so its synchronised level is inverted before debouncing
AIM.149.reason: With OTP_trig low (normal temperature), OTP_sync_db asserts after the 1 ms qualification. The supervisor then stays in S_OFF with En low and Red_LED2 lit, and a real over-temperature (OTP_trig high) is what lets it start.

AIM.150.description: The output-rail window comparator is taken as an active-low power-fail output, so pgood_gen is handed its inverted synchronised level
AIM.150.reason: In S_RUN with PGOOD_comp high (rail in regulation), PGOOD and switch_supply stay low. With the comparator low (rail out of window), PGOOD asserts once the qualifying cycles have passed, so the changeover moves onto a rail that has failed.

AIM.151.description: The physical enable switch is treated as active low (a switch to ground with a pull-up), so its synchronised level is inverted before the 20 ms debouncer
AIM.151.reason: With en_from_switch low (switch off), the debounced enable asserts after 20 ms and the supervisor starts the converter (En high, soft start). Turning the switch on shuts it down. reg_file's switch status bit and the press edge detector are inverted too.

AIM.152.description: fault_arbiter is handed the RUN trip threshold minus one, as if it tripped on count > trip_run, though it already compares with >=
AIM.152.reason: In S_RUN, a window holding 11 faulted valley samples out of 16 (one below the default TRIP_RUN of 12) raises window_trip. The supervisor goes to S_HICCUP and a strike is counted, where the design keeps running.

AIM.153.description: The fault-log timestamp is held in reset whenever the gate driver is disabled, reading 'time since start of convertor' as time since the converter was enabled, though the timestamp must free-run in every state and be cleared only by rst_n
AIM.153.reason: In S_OFF and S_HICCUP, and on the very clock a hard fault drops En, timestamp_ms is held at zero. The live TIME registers read 0 while the converter is off, and fault_cause's episode-start snapshot of a shutdown fault records 0 instead of the elapsed time.

AIM.154.description: Master_PWM from the modulator is taken as active low (as if it were the low-side drive command), so it is inverted before its synchroniser
AIM.154.reason: Every block then sees the off-time as the on-time. pwm_mask passes PWM_out high while Osc_in is low, the valley CP sample and the cycle boundaries move to the opposite edge, and DUTY_COUNT reports the complement of the real duty.

AIM.155.description: hiccup_timer is handed hiccup_base minus one, an off-by-one 'fix' for its counter matching at the target, which shortens every cool-down by 2**strike_level clocks
AIM.155.reason: After each entry into S_HICCUP, hiccup_done rises and the supervisor re-enters S_SS (En high) 2**strike_level clocks earlier than the programmed base shifted by the strike level.

AIM.156.description: fault_arbiter's soft-start scope also covers S_HICCUP, as if the cool-down and its soft-start retry were one episode, so the overcurrent windows and the CP history are not cleared during the hiccup
AIM.156.reason: fault_arbiter clears its windows only when neither of its state inputs is high, so with this change a hiccup no longer wipes them. After a RUN window trip, the RUN count stays at or above trip_run through the cool-down and the retry ramp, so the converter goes straight back to S_HICCUP (En drops, another strike, and eventually latch_out) on the first clock of S_RUN. After a soft-start trip, window_trip_SS is still high when S_SS is re-entered, so the retry trips again at once.

AIM.157.description: The supervisor's switch enable is ANDed with the raw synchronised switch, following a 'switch-off must act at once' idea, so only the press is debounced and a release or bounce takes effect immediately
AIM.157.reason: Turning the switch on still waits the full 20 ms qualification. But when the switch is released, or bounces low for even one clock while the converter is in S_SS or S_RUN, En drops and the FSM goes to S_OFF straight away, not 20 ms later. The reg_file switch status stays at its debounced value the whole time.

AIM.158.description: spi_slave is held in reset whenever the filtered chip select is high, meant to stop noise on a deselected bus from disturbing it, so a transaction's end at CS rise is erased before the slave can judge it
AIM.158.reason: When CS rises, the reset asserts on the same clock edge, so spi_slave never registers cs_rise and never pulses integrity_ok or txn_abort. No host write ever commits: CONTROL, SCRATCH and thresholds stay unchanged and the bus-error count stays at zero. Reads still work.

AIM.159.description: strike_counter is reset whenever the debounced enable switch is off, as if cycling the switch earned a fresh set of strikes, though latch_assert must be cleared only by rst_n together with the physical SCR
AIM.159.reason: After a strike latch has tripped, turning the switch off drops the latch_out pin and zeroes strike_level (Red_LED1 blink, STRIKE_LEVEL register) while the SCR stays set. Strikes left over from earlier hiccups are also lost on any switch-off, so the hiccup escalation restarts.

AIM.160.description: fault_cause's record is also cleared by a fresh press of the enable switch, taking an 'episode' to mean one power-on run instead of one host read window
AIM.160.reason: A host that reads the FAULT_CAUSE/FTIME registers after the user switched the board off and back on finds the record and its start time zeroed. The cause of the shutdown is lost before it was ever read.

AIM.161.description: The switch-press pulse en_switch_rise is registered, so it reaches reg_file one clock after the debounced switch rises instead of on the same clock
AIM.161.before: always_comb begin /  / /* / Purpose: Edge detection on the physical enable switch signal synced and debounced / */ /  / en_switch_rise = ~en_from_switch_sync_db_d & en_from_switch_sync_db;
AIM.161.after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin /  / /* / Purpose: Edge detection on the physical enable switch signal synced and debounced / */ /  / if (!rst_n) en_switch_rise <= 1'b0; / else        en_switch_rise <= ~en_from_switch_sync_db_d & en_from_switch_sync_db;
AIM.161.reason: With a host veto in force, pressing the switch restores spi_enable one clock late. So the supervisor leaves S_OFF and raises En one clock later than the debounced switch allows. A host CONTROL commit landing on the following clock now resolves the same-clock collision the other way.

AIM.162.description: The valley-current comparator is mistaken for a peak current limit, so pwm_mask's PWM is cut on any clock where CP_trig is high, a cycle-by-cycle limit the design does not have
AIM.162.reason: In S_SS or S_RUN, if CP_trig goes high during a high-side on-time, PWM_out falls at once instead of following the modulator pulse up to the soft_start ceiling. The design only counts CP_trig per cycle in fault_arbiter's window and never truncates a pulse with it.

AIM.163.description: The supervisor's hiccup exit also waits for the synchronised valley-current comparator to clear, 'do not retry into a live overcurrent', although the header says a retry always follows hiccup_done
AIM.163.reason: If CP_trig stays high through S_HICCUP (a persistent overcurrent or short), the FSM never goes back to S_SS. En stays low, no more strikes build up, and latch_out never asserts. The design instead retries after the cool-down and latches on the third strike.

AIM.164.description: fault_LED shows outstanding strikes only while the supervisor is in S_RUN, taking 'blink through the clean-run window' to mean only that, so Red_LED1 does not blink during the hiccup cool-down or the soft-start retry
AIM.164.reason: With strike_level non-zero and no latch, Red_LED1 is held low in S_HICCUP and S_SS. It should follow the 4 Hz blink there, and this shows once the blink timebase has toggled (after 125 ms of run time). It blinks again only after S_RUN is re-entered.

AIM.165.description: The fault-log timestamp is restarted each time the host finishes reading the fault record (fault_reg_read_done), taking the timestamp to be time since the last episode, though it must free-run from rst_n
AIM.165.reason: Once the host has read through FTIME_2 (0x20), the TIME_0..2 registers read near zero instead of the time since reset. Every later fault_time snapshot is also measured from that read, not from start-up.

AIM.166.description: reg_file is held in reset while the debounced enable switch is off, as if switching off were a full reset of the host configuration
AIM.166.reason: Host writes to thresholds, CONTROL or SCRATCH are lost while the switch is off. Turning the switch off after configuring puts trip_run, trip_ss, max_strikes, max_on_limit and the rest back to their package defaults, and clears a host disable veto (spi_enable back to 1).

AIM.167.description: The supervisor's over-temperature input ORs the undebounced synchronised OTP flag with the debounced one ('trip at once, debounce only the release'), so the 1 ms assert qualification no longer applies to the FSM
AIM.167.reason: An OTP_trig glitch of only a few clocks pulls En low combinationally and sends the FSM to S_OFF, so the converter restarts through soft start. The design rides through glitches shorter than 1 ms.

AIM.168.description: soft_start's ramp runs through the hiccup cool-down as well as S_SS, as if cool-down plus retry were one ramp period, so the ceiling keeps widening while the gate driver is off
AIM.168.reason: The modulator keeps switching during S_HICCUP, so the ceiling (and SS_done) climbs during the cool-down. The retry then starts above MIN_ON_COUNTS, or the FSM leaves S_SS for S_RUN at once, and PWM_out pulses are wide right after re-enable instead of re-ramping from the floor.

AIM.169.description: Master_PWM goes through the short symmetric SPI glitch filter after its synchroniser, as if switch-node pickup on the modulator line needed the same 160 ns filter as SCK, so every block's cycle reference is delayed and short pulses are swallowed
AIM.169.after: logic Osc_sync_raw; / input_sync u_osc_sync (.clk(clk), .rst_n(rst_n), .async_in(Osc_in), .sync_out(Osc_sync_raw)); / input_debounce #(.ASSERT_CLKS(SPI_FILTER_CLKS), .RELEASE_CLKS(SPI_FILTER_CLKS), .RESET_VALUE(1'b0)) / u_osc_filt (.clk(clk), .rst_n(rst_n), .flag_in(Osc_sync_raw), .flag_out(Osc_sync));
AIM.169.reason: PWM_out now lags Osc_in by 8 more clocks than it should. Any modulator high or low pulse shorter than 8 clocks (160 ns) disappears from PWM_out and from the cycle counts in fault_arbiter, soft_start, pgood_gen and pwm_stats, which also changes the DUTY_COUNT and period telemetry for narrow pulses.

AIM.170.description: fault_arbiter's valley-sample lookback BLANK_CLKS is sized from the LM5106 turn-on shrinkage (7 clocks, 140 ns), as if the blanking had to cover the gate driver's delay, instead of the module's 5-clock (100 ns) default
AIM.170.reason: Each per-cycle valley sample at the PWM rising edge now reads CP_trig as it was 7 clocks before turn-on instead of 5. A comparator assertion that starts 5-6 clocks before turn-on is no longer counted, and one that clears in that interval is still counted. This changes when window_trip / window_trip_SS fire, and so the En shutdown into hiccup and the FAULT_COUNT telemetry.

AIM.171.description: pwm_mask's on-time ceiling has the LM5106 turn-on shrinkage added at the call site, so the gate on-time is meant to equal the ceiling, but the shrinkage is then counted twice because MIN_ON_COUNTS already includes it
AIM.171.reason: Every PWM_out pulse is now cut 7 clocks later than the ceiling soft_start produces. During soft start the floor pulse is 19 clocks instead of 12 and each ramp step is offset the same way. In S_RUN, pulses of 84-90 clocks pass where the 75% backstop should truncate them.

AIM.172.description: soft_start's ramp branch is enabled only while the ramp is unfinished (ss_active and not SS_done), as if a finished ramp no longer needed the S_SS branch, so on the last S_SS clock it falls into the reset-to-floor branch
AIM.172.reason: On the clock after SS_done sets, the supervisor is still in S_SS, so soft_start resets max_on_counts to the 12-clock floor and clears SS_done while the FSM moves to S_RUN. soft_start then holds that floor through S_RUN, and PWM_out is cut to the floor on-time for the whole run instead of the max_on_limit ceiling.

AIM.173.description: fault_arbiter is handed the soft-start trip threshold minus one, as if it tripped on count > trip_ss, though it already compares with >=
AIM.173.reason: In S_SS, window_trip_SS and the S_SS -> S_HICCUP exit (En dropping) now fire when 27 of the last 32 valley samples are faulted instead of 28. A host-written TRIP_SS is also one cycle short.

AIM.174.description: fault_cause is held in reset while the gate driver is disabled, so routine power-downs do not log a fault. This wipes the record on every fault shutdown, which is exactly when it must survive.
AIM.174.reason: A fault in S_SS or S_RUN drops En at once (combinationally for OTP, UVLO and latch, or by entering S_HICCUP or S_OFF), so the cause captured on that clock is cleared. FAULT_REG and FAULT_TIME read back zero over SPI after any shutdown, instead of holding the cause until the host reads it.

AIM.175.description: fault_LED's over-temperature input is gated by 'converter running' like fault_cause's capture gate, though the LEDs show what is wrong now and must light in any state
AIM.175.reason: When OTP asserts in S_RUN the supervisor goes to S_OFF on the next clock, so Red_LED2 lights for at most a clock and then stays dark while the board is still over-temperature. With OTP present in S_OFF it never lights at all.

AIM.176.description: The switch-press pulse is taken as a rise of the combined enable (switch AND host CONTROL enable), so it is masked exactly when the host has disabled the converter, which is the one case the press is there to override
AIM.176.reason: After a host CONTROL write clears spi_enable, cycling the physical switch no longer raises en_switch_rise, so reg_file does not set spi_enable again and En stays low after the press. In the original, the press brings the converter back up through S_SS.

AIM.177.description: fault_arbiter's soft-start scope is limited to the unfinished ramp (S_SS and not SS_done), so on the last S_SS clock it sees neither state active and clears both windows and the CP history
AIM.177.reason: On the one clock when SS_done is high in S_SS, window_trip_SS is held low, so a trip landing then sends the FSM to S_RUN instead of S_HICCUP. fault_count_ss is also cleared, so the soft-start fault count that reg_file should show through S_RUN reads 0.

AIM.178.description: The supervisor holds in S_SS after the ramp is done until the live valley-current comparator is clear, treating 'do not hand over to RUN in overcurrent' as a condition of the ramp handshake
AIM.178.reason: If CP_trig is high when SS_done asserts, the FSM stays in S_SS instead of going to S_RUN, so PGOOD qualification starts later. Overcurrent is then judged against the more tolerant trip_ss instead of trip_run.
