AIM.179.description: reg_file's commit and discard strobes are qualified by chip select still asserted, though spi_slave raises both only after CS has risen at the end of the transaction
AIM.179.reason: integrity_ok and txn_abort pulse the clock after cs_rise, while cs_n_filt is already high, so no host write ever commits. A CONTROL disable or a threshold change never takes effect, and the bus-error count never increments.

AIM.180.description: soft_start's ramp target is floored at the 75% default ceiling, from the package rule that the digital mask must stay above the analog clamp and never be the primary limiter, so a host-lowered MAX_ON limit is overridden
AIM.180.reason: If the host writes MAX_ON (0x53) below 37 counts, the next soft start should end with SS_done at the written ceiling and PWM_out pulses cut there. With this fault the ramp keeps climbing to 37, SS_done asserts later, and PWM_out on-times in S_SS and S_RUN stay wider than the host commanded.

AIM.181.description: fault_arbiter's soft-start trip threshold is floored at the RUN threshold, enforcing the package note that S_SS is 'more tolerant', so a legal host write of trip_ss below trip_run is overridden
AIM.181.reason: Suppose the host writes TRIP_SS (0x51) below TRIP_RUN, e.g. 5 against 12. An overcurrent in S_SS with 5 to 11 faulted cycles in the window should raise window_trip_SS and send the FSM to S_HICCUP, dropping En and counting a strike. With this fault the converter keeps soft-starting until 12 faulted cycles.

AIM.182.description: The supervisor's host enable is ORed with the switch-press pulse at the top level, so a fresh press overrides a host disable on the press clock itself. reg_file already restores spi_enable on the next clock, so the override lands a clock early.
AIM.182.reason: Take a host that has disabled the converter over SPI, and then the switch is pressed. The FSM should leave S_OFF, and En rise, one clock after reg_file registers spi_enable high. With this fault both happen one clock earlier, while CONTROL/STATUS still read spi_enable low.

AIM.186.description: fault_LED's UVLO indication is masked unless the converter is in S_SS or S_RUN. This borrows fault_cause's 'a routine power-down asserts UVLO' capture rule, but the LEDs must show what is wrong now, in every state.
AIM.186.reason: With UVLO_trig asserted while the supervisor is in S_OFF or S_HICCUP, for example at power-up on a low input rail, Red_LED3 stays dark instead of lighting. A UVLO that hits in S_RUN lights it for only one clock before the FSM leaves S_RUN.

AIM.187.description: The switch-press pulse is suppressed while the host enable is still set, as if it were only needed to lift a veto already in place. reg_file's rule that the physical switch wins a same-clock collision with a host disable is lost.
AIM.187.reason: When the debounced switch rises on the same clock that a validated CONTROL disable commits, spi_enable is still 1, so the press is masked and the disable lands. The converter stays off (En low, STATUS bit 5 clear) instead of the press keeping it enabled.

AIM.188.description: pgood_gen's 'regulating' qualifier also drops on the RUN window trip. The aim is to hand the rail back the moment an overcurrent is detected, but PGOOD should follow the supervisor's exit from S_RUN.
AIM.188.reason: On a RUN overcurrent window trip, PGOOD and switch_supply fall on the trip clock, one clock before the supervisor leaves S_RUN for S_HICCUP, and the qualifying count is cleared a clock early.

AIM.189.description: The overcurrent window trips are folded into fault_LED's running indication, a second path that fault_LED's header deliberately leaves out because the supervisor's state change already turns off the green LED.
AIM.189.reason: On a soft-start or RUN window trip, Green_LED turns off one clock earlier than when it follows the supervisor's exit to S_HICCUP.

AIM.190.description: hiccup_timer's cool-down counter is sized from the default 5 ms base instead of the largest legal host-written base (HICCUP_BASE_MAX_CLKS), which is the sizing mistake the package warns against
AIM.190.reason: Suppose the host writes a hiccup base above about 10.5 ms, which is legal up to 20 ms. On a strike of 1 or more, base<<strike_level then overflows the 20-bit target and wraps to a smaller value, so the cool-down ends early and En comes back on before the commanded interval.

AIM.191.description: fault_cause's RUN overcurrent input is wired to the soft-start window trip, so both of its overcurrent inputs carry window_trip_SS and a RUN window trip is never logged
AIM.191.reason: When an overcurrent window trip in S_RUN sends the converter into hiccup, the overcurrent bit of FAULT_CAUSE is not set and no episode timestamp is latched. A host read then shows an empty or incomplete fault record. Soft-start trips are still logged.

AIM.192.description: reg_file's STRIKE_LEVEL telemetry is zeroed once the CPLD's strike latch has tripped, copying fault_LED's 'latch outranks strikes' priority into the register map. strike_counter deliberately keeps the count readable after latching.
AIM.192.reason: Once the third hiccup trips latch_out, a host read of STRIKE_LEVEL returns 0 instead of the accumulated count of 3. Before the latch trips the value read is unchanged.

AIM.193.description: reg_file's FCOUNT_SS telemetry is gated by S_SS, mirroring the way fault_arbiter gates window_trip_SS by its own state. But the soft-start count is meant to stay frozen, and readable, through S_RUN.
AIM.193.reason: Suppose some valley-current cycles are counted during soft start without tripping. A host that reads FCOUNT_SS in S_RUN then gets 0 instead of the frozen soft-start count fault_arbiter still holds.

AIM.194.description: The switch-press pulse that restores the host enable is ignored while a debounced OTP or UVLO is live, as if a press should only re-enable a board that is able to start.
AIM.194.reason: Take a host that has cleared CONTROL's enable. If the user toggles the switch on during over-temperature or undervoltage, spi_enable is not restored. When the fault clears, the converter stays in S_OFF and CONTROL still reads disabled, where it should restart.

AIM.195.description: UVLO is only qualified while the gate driver is enabled. This borrows the 'a routine power-down asserts UVLO' rule to ignore UVLO when not switching, so the debounced UVLO the FSM sees drops in S_OFF.
AIM.195.reason: With UVLO_trig held high and the board enabled, UVLO_sync_db releases 200 us after shutdown. The supervisor then leaves S_OFF for S_SS into an undervoltage input and cycles on and off. Red_LED3 also goes dark in S_OFF while UVLO is still asserted.

AIM.196.description: fault_cause's clear-on-read is suppressed while the converter is in S_SS or S_RUN, meant to avoid wiping an episode still in progress. The record and its fault_time then survive a host read that should close the read window.
AIM.196.reason: Say a fault has been recorded and the host reads the record through 0x20 while the converter is running. The cause byte and the FTIME bytes are not cleared, so the next read returns the stale causes and the old episode-start time, where it should return a fresh, empty record.

AIM.197.description: fault_LED's blink half-period is overridden with the full 250 ms period of the intended 4 Hz blink, so the period is mistaken for the half-period.
AIM.197.reason: While strikes are outstanding and no latch is set, Red_LED1 toggles every 250 ms (a 2 Hz blink) instead of every 125 ms. A board recovering through its roughly 1 s clean-run window then shows only two blink cycles.

AIM.198.description: The FAULT_FLAGS current-protection status bit is masked while the modulator PWM is high, on the idea that the valley comparator only means something during low-side conduction.
AIM.198.reason: A host read of FAULT_FLAGS shows the CP bit clear whenever the synchronised Osc_in is high, even though CP_trig is asserted. With the modulator held high, or a read landing in the on-time, a live overcurrent comparator is not reported.

AIM.199.description: reg_file's UVLO status bit is masked outside S_SS and S_RUN, copying fault_cause's 'a routine power-down asserts UVLO' capture rule into the live status register.
AIM.199.reason: In S_OFF with the debounced UVLO asserted (for example after reset with the input rail low), FAULT_FLAGS reads UVLO clear even though UVLO is what holds the supervisor off. The host cannot see why the converter will not start.

AIM.200.description: strike_counter's clean-run streak is also broken whenever the output comparator reports the rail out of window, so 'fault-free running' is taken to need the rail in regulation as well as no overcurrent window trip.
AIM.200.reason: In S_RUN with PGOOD_comp low, or dipping now and then, the clean-run counter keeps restarting. strike_level then never clears after clean_run_target cycles: STRIKE_LEVEL stays non-zero, Red_LED1 keeps blinking and the next hiccup cool-down is longer than it should be.

AIM.201.description: pgood_gen treats a live valley-current comparator as 'rail not good', so any CP_trig assertion in S_RUN clears the power-good qualification
AIM.201.reason: In S_RUN with the output comparator good, any clock with the synchronised CP_trig high, even far below the window trip count, drops PGOOD and switch_supply at once. They then stay low for the full 9 ms requalification, though the supervisor never leaves S_RUN.

AIM.202.description: pgood_gen is qualified on S_RUN with no strikes outstanding, as if the housekeeping rail must not be handed to a converter still proving itself after a hiccup
AIM.202.reason: After a hiccup retry reaches S_RUN with a good rail, PGOOD and switch_supply stay low through the whole clean-run window and only qualify after strike_counter clears strike_level. Unmutated, they assert after the 9 ms qualification.

AIM.203.description: The debounced over-temperature flag is added as a second CPLD trip source into the shared SCR latch, as if OTP were a hard fault to latch, instead of latch_out following strike_counter's latch_assert alone
AIM.203.after: logic strike_latch_assert; / strike_counter u_strike_counter ( .clk(clk), / .rst_n(rst_n), / .max_strikes(max_strikes), / .clean_run_target(clean_run_target), / .pwm_sync(Osc_sync), / .hiccup_active(hiccup_active), / .run_active(run_active), / .window_trip(window_trip), / .strike_level(strike_level), / .latch_assert(strike_latch_assert) / ); / assign latch_out = strike_latch_assert | OTP_sync_db;
AIM.203.reason: A debounced OTP drives latch_out high in any state, with no strikes counted. The supervisor and fault_LED then see latch_assert, so Red_LED1 goes solid and fault_cause logs a LATCH cause where only OTP should show.

AIM.204.description: fault_LED's running indication is suppressed while strikes are outstanding, so Green_LED is not lit together with the blinking Red_LED1 during the clean-run window
AIM.204.reason: After a hiccup, Green_LED stays dark through the retry's soft start and S_RUN until strike_level is cleared. fault_LED's header requires green to be lit alongside the strike blink while the board runs and proves itself.

AIM.205.description: pgood_gen gets the inverted modulator PWM, so it counts its qualifying cycles at high-side turn-on (the cycle boundary fault_arbiter uses) instead of at the end of each pulse
AIM.205.reason: In S_RUN with the rail in window, PGOOD and switch_supply rise on a PWM rising edge instead of a falling one, so the moment they assert moves by the PWM on-time. The PGOOD qualifying count also starts from a different edge after each entry into S_RUN.

AIM.206.description: strike_counter counts a strike on the overcurrent window trip itself instead of on entry into S_HICCUP, as if 'a strike' were the trip rather than the hiccup it causes
AIM.206.reason: strike_level and latch_out change one clock early, on the clock the FSM leaves S_SS/S_RUN rather than the clock after it enters S_HICCUP. A trip on the same clock as a hard fault (OTP, UVLO, switch off) sends the FSM to S_OFF, yet a strike is still counted, so later hiccups are longer and latch_out trips early.

AIM.207.description: MISO is retimed through an extra clk flop 'to deglitch it', though the header says both terms are already flops and MISO is driven straight from them
AIM.207.after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin / if (!rst_n) begin MISO <= 1'b0; end / else begin MISO <= sdio_oe & sdio_out; end / end
AIM.207.reason: Every MISO transition during a read comes one clk later than spi_slave's shift edge. On deselect, MISO stays high for one extra clock after sdio_oe has dropped.

AIM.208.description: fault_LED is held in reset while the debounced enable switch is off, as if a switched-off board should show a dark front panel. The LEDs must show what is wrong now, in every state.
AIM.208.reason: With the enable switch off, a live debounced OTP, UVLO or SCR latch read-back no longer lights Red_LED2, Red_LED3 or Red_LED1. They stay dark until the switch has been on for 20 ms, and the blink timebase restarts on each switch-on.

AIM.209.description: reg_file is instanced with its two magic key bytes swapped: DISABLE_KEY is set to the write-access value 0xA7 and WRITE_ACCESS_KEY to the disable value 0xD1
AIM.209.reason: The documented sequence, 0xD1 to DISABLE_KEY then CONTROL bit 0 cleared, no longer arms the disable, so spi_enable and En stay high. 0xD1 at 0x4F no longer unlocks the threshold bank, so a keyed threshold write sets write_rejected and leaves the thresholds unchanged.

AIM.210.description: The timestamp prescaler is handed PRESCALE_VAL minus one, an off-by-one 'fix' made at the call site although timestamp already compares its prescaler with PRESCALE_VAL-1
AIM.210.reason: The millisecond tick comes every 49999 clocks instead of 50000, so timestamp_ms runs fast by one clock per tick. TIME_0..2, the fault_time snapshot and the 5 s host watchdog drift, and a read near a tick boundary returns a count one higher than the true elapsed milliseconds.

AIM.211.description: latch_out is retimed through an extra output flop 'because it drives the SCR gate', though the header says it is driven straight from strike_counter's latch_assert
AIM.211.after: logic latch_assert_q;   // strike_counter's latch_assert, before the output register / strike_counter u_strike_counter ( .clk(clk), / .rst_n(rst_n), / .max_strikes(max_strikes), / .clean_run_target(clean_run_target), / .pwm_sync(Osc_sync), / .hiccup_active(hiccup_active), / .run_active(run_active), / .window_trip(window_trip), / .strike_level(strike_level), / .latch_assert(latch_assert_q) / ); / always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin / if (!rst_n) begin latch_out <= 1'b0; end / else begin latch_out <= latch_assert_q; end / end
AIM.211.reason: On the hiccup entry that reaches the strike limit, latch_out rises one clock late. The supervisor, fault_cause and fault_LED, which all read latch_out, also see the CPLD's strike latch a clock later, so the Red_LED1 solid indication is a clock late too.

AIM.212.description: The gate PWM gets a second pin register at the top level for glitch-free output, although pwm_mask's output is already a flop
AIM.212.after: logic pwm_mask_out;   // pwm_mask's masked PWM, before the pin register / pwm_mask u_pwm_mask ( .clk(clk), / .rst_n(rst_n), / .pwm_sync(Osc_sync), / .max_on_counts(max_on_counts), / .pwm_out(pwm_mask_out) / ); / always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin / if (!rst_n) begin PWM_out <= 1'b0; end / else begin PWM_out <= pwm_mask_out; end / end
AIM.212.reason: Both edges of every PWM_out pulse lag Osc_in by one more clock than designed. This includes the truncated edge where the on-time ceiling cuts a long pulse, so the gate drive runs one clock behind the modulator in S_SS and S_RUN.

AIM.213.description: spi_slave's SCK falling edge is taken straight from the unfiltered synchronised SCK, so only the rising (sampling) edge goes through the glitch filter, as if only the sample edge needed filtering
AIM.213.reason: sck_fall now comes 8 clocks earlier than the filtered rising edge, so MISO changes 160 ns earlier in each bit. A short low glitch on SCK during its high phase now makes a false fall and rise, which shifts an extra bit and corrupts the frame (CRC fail and txn_abort on a write, wrong read data).

AIM.214.description: reg_file's timestamp snapshot is only taken for reads that begin inside the TIME bank (0x18-0x1A), though rd_first must freeze it at the start of any read
AIM.214.reason: A burst read that starts below 0x18, for example at STATUS 0x10, and sweeps through 0x18-0x1A returns the snapshot left by an earlier read, or 0 after reset, instead of the current timestamp.

AIM.215.description: The dead-master SCK idle timeout is given the 5 s host-silence watchdog interval (WD_TIMEOUT_MS) instead of its own 2 ms
AIM.215.reason: If the master stops clocking with CS still low, the slave reaches S_DEAD only after 5 s, not 2 ms. During a read MISO keeps showing read data that long, and a stalled write is not poisoned in that time.

AIM.216.description: reg_file's FAULT_TIME registers are given the age of the episode (timestamp_ms minus the episode-start snapshot) instead of the episode-start time itself, reading 'timestamp of the fault' as 'time since the fault'
AIM.216.reason: A host reading FTIME_0..2 after a logged fault gets a value that grows with every read instead of the frozen start time. With no fault logged (fault_time cleared to 0) it reads the live timestamp instead of zero.

AIM.217.description: fault_LED's 'strikes outstanding' is taken to mean strikes remaining before the latch (max_strikes - strike_level) instead of strikes accumulated
AIM.217.reason: After reset, with no strikes and the default nonzero strike limit, Red_LED1 blinks although nothing has happened. Once the accumulated count reaches the limit the blink stops unless a latch makes the LED solid.

AIM.218.description: The CPLD's trip drive latch_out is held on while the debounced SCR read-back is set, as if the gate drive had to sustain the SCR, instead of following strike_counter's latch_assert alone
AIM.218.after: logic sc_latch_assert; / strike_counter u_strike_counter ( .clk(clk), / .rst_n(rst_n), / .max_strikes(max_strikes), / .clean_run_target(clean_run_target), / .pwm_sync(Osc_sync), / .hiccup_active(hiccup_active), / .run_active(run_active), / .window_trip(window_trip), / .strike_level(strike_level), / .latch_assert(sc_latch_assert) / ); / assign latch_out = sc_latch_assert | latch_stat_sync_db;
AIM.218.reason: When the analog OVP fires the SCR, latch_out goes high and stays high until reset, though the CPLD never tripped. fault_cause then sees latch_assert set and stops logging the event as OVP.

AIM.219.description: The supervisor ignores input undervoltage during soft start, as if input-rail sag from the start-up inrush were expected and had to be blanked
AIM.219.reason: If a debounced UVLO occurs in S_SS, En stays high and the FSM does not go to S_OFF. The converter keeps switching until it reaches S_RUN, although the header says UVLO forces S_OFF from every state.

AIM.220.description: Host write data is bit-reversed before reg_file, as if spi_slave assembled bytes LSB-first, though the bus is MSB-first
AIM.220.reason: Every host write lands bit-reversed. A threshold write sets the wrong value, and the key bytes no longer match (0xA7 arrives as 0xE5), so unlock and disable writes fail. Reads are not affected.

AIM.221.description: The hiccup_done handshake from hiccup_timer is registered once more at the top level before the supervisor, so the cool-down end is acted on one clock late
AIM.221.after: logic hiccup_done_tmr; / hiccup_timer u_hiccup_timer ( .clk(clk), / .rst_n(rst_n), / .base_clks(hiccup_base), / .hiccup_active(hiccup_active), / .strike_level(strike_level), / .hiccup_done(hiccup_done_tmr) / ); / always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin / if (!rst_n) hiccup_done <= 1'b0; / else        hiccup_done <= hiccup_done_tmr; / end
AIM.221.reason: Each hiccup cool-down lasts one clock longer than base << strike_level, so En rises again for the soft-start retry one clock later than it should.

AIM.222.description: A completed ramp outranks a soft-start overcurrent trip: window_trip_SS is masked by SS_done at the supervisor, so a same-clock trip hands over to S_RUN instead of hiccuping
AIM.222.reason: If window_trip_SS asserts on the clock SS_done rises, the FSM goes to S_RUN with En held high instead of to S_HICCUP. The trip is lost, because window_trip_SS is only produced in S_SS, so there is no hiccup and no strike.

AIM.223.description: soft_start's SS_done handshake is registered once more at the top level before the supervisor, so the end of the ramp is acted on one clock late
AIM.223.after: logic SS_done_q; / always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin / if (!rst_n) SS_done_q <= 1'b0; / else        SS_done_q <= SS_done; / end / supervisor u_supervisor ( .clk(clk), / .SS_done(SS_done_q),
AIM.223.reason: Every S_SS to S_RUN changeover happens one clock later, so run_active, PGOOD qualification and the Green_LED/state telemetry move a clock. After a quick S_RUN to S_OFF to S_SS sequence, the stale registered SS_done can also send a fresh soft start straight to S_RUN without ramping.

AIM.224.description: fault_arbiter's RUN window trip is retimed through a flop before the supervisor to break the counter-compare path, so the S_RUN to S_HICCUP exit lands one clock after the trip
AIM.224.after: logic window_trip_q; / always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin / if (!rst_n) window_trip_q <= 1'b0; / else        window_trip_q <= window_trip; / end / supervisor u_supervisor ( .clk(clk), / .SS_done(SS_done), / .rst_n(rst_n), / .en_SW(en_from_switch_sync_db), / .spi_enable(spi_enable), / .latch_state(latch_stat_sync_db), / .OTP(OTP_sync_db), / .window_trip_SS(window_trip_SS), / .window_trip(window_trip_q),
AIM.224.reason: When the RUN overcurrent window trips, En stays high and the gate keeps switching for one extra clock. The hiccup entry, the strike increment and the cool-down start all happen a clock later.

AIM.225.description: spi_slave's combinational rd_first is registered before reg_file as an ordinary strobe, so the read snapshot is taken one clock after the first read byte has already been loaded
AIM.225.after: / logic rd_first_q; / always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin / if (!rst_n) rd_first_q <= 1'b0; / else        rd_first_q <= spi_rd_first; / end / reg_file u_reg_file ( .clk(clk), / .rst_n(rst_n), /  / // host access port / .addr(spi_addr), / .wr_en(spi_wr_en), / .wdata(spi_wdata), / .rdata(spi_rdata), / .rd_first(rd_first_q),
AIM.225.reason: In a read that starts in the TIME bank, the first byte is served from the previous read's timestamp snapshot instead of the live value. The following bytes come from the new snapshot, so a multi-byte TIME read tears.

AIM.226.description: FAULT_CAUSE is read through a priority encoder that keeps only the highest set cause bit, from reading 'priority is encoded in bit position' as 'report the top cause only', though the record is a one-hot OR accumulation
AIM.226.reason: When an episode records two causes, for example OTP and UVLO both live while running, a host read of 0x1D shows only the higher bit instead of both.

AIM.227.description: The FAULT_FLAGS over-temperature bit ORs in fault_cause's recorded OTP cause, making the live status flag sticky like the fault record
AIM.227.reason: After an over-temperature in S_SS/S_RUN has cleared, FAULT_FLAGS bit 1 still reads 1 until the host reads 0x20 and the record clears, instead of following the debounced OTP flag.

AIM.228.description: The fault record is also cleared by a write to FAULT_CAUSE (0x1D), applying the write-1-to-clear convention to a register that is read-only and clears on read
AIM.228.reason: A host write burst that touches 0x1D wipes fault_reg and fault_time, even though that address is read-only and the write is rejected, so the next read of the record comes back empty.

AIM.229.description: The supervisor ignores over-temperature during S_HICCUP, on the idea that the cool-down already holds the gate off and the retry will catch it
AIM.229.reason: An OTP that asserts during a hiccup cool-down leaves the FSM in S_HICCUP instead of sending it to S_OFF. The state read back over SPI and the restart timing change: the retry follows hiccup_done instead of the OTP release.

AIM.230.description: pgood_gen's qualifying count is given the delay in milliseconds (PGOOD_DELAY_MS = 9) where it expects switching cycles, so a unit conversion is left out
AIM.230.reason: PGOOD and switch_supply assert after 9 good switching cycles (about 20 us) in S_RUN instead of 4050 (9 ms), so the housekeeping rail is handed over before the output has settled.

AIM.231.description: soft_start's ramp floor is given the summed floor in nanoseconds (240) without ns_to_clks, so a value in ns is used as a clk count
AIM.231.reason: The truncated floor (112 counts) is above the 83-count limit. Every soft start clamps to the limit and asserts SS_done on its first clock with no ramp, and outside S_SS/S_RUN pwm_mask's ceiling is 112 counts instead of 12.

AIM.232.description: Register read data is bit-reversed before spi_slave, as if the slave shifted MISO out LSB-first, though the bus is MSB-first
AIM.232.after: .sdio_oe(sdio_oe), / .addr(spi_addr), / .wr_en(spi_wr_en), / .wdata(spi_wdata), / .rdata({spi_rdata[0], spi_rdata[1], spi_rdata[2], spi_rdata[3], spi_rdata[4], spi_rdata[5], spi_rdata[6], spi_rdata[7]}),
AIM.232.reason: Every register read the host makes comes back bit-reversed on MISO. For example PMIC_ID 0xB5 reads as 0xAD, and the read CRC no longer covers the bytes the host sees.

AIM.233.description: The free-running timestamp reaches reg_file with its three bytes in reverse order, so TIME_0 at 0x18 holds the most significant byte instead of the least
AIM.233.reason: After the first millisecond tick, a read of TIME_0..TIME_2 returns the timestamp bytes swapped end for end. reg_file's host-silence watchdog also does its arithmetic on this non-monotonic value, so its timeout moves.

AIM.234.description: fault_cause's episode-start time reaches reg_file byte-reversed, so FTIME_0 at 0x1E reports the most significant byte
AIM.234.reason: Once a fault has been logged at a nonzero timestamp, reading FTIME_0..FTIME_2 gives the start-time bytes in the wrong order.

AIM.235.description: The one-hot fault-cause record is wired to reg_file bit-reversed, as if bit 0 were the highest-priority cause, so OC appears in the OVP position and OVP in the OC position
AIM.235.reason: After any logged fault other than OTP, a read of FAULT_CAUSE (0x1D) reports the wrong cause bit. For example, a RUN overcurrent hiccup reads as bit 4 (OVP) instead of bit 0.

AIM.236.description: strike_counter is given the strike limit plus one, as if MAX_STRIKES counted the hiccups allowed before the latching strike rather than the latching strike itself
AIM.236.reason: If the host writes MAX_STRIKES to 1 or 2, latch_out asserts one hiccup later than configured. At the default of 3 the sum wraps in STRIKE_W bits, so the latching point moves too.

AIM.237.description: run_active is retimed through a flop before pgood_gen to break the supervisor-to-PGOOD path, so the power-good qualifier lags the FSM by a clock
AIM.237.after: logic run_active_q; / always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin / if (!rst_n) begin run_active_q <= 1'b0; end / else begin run_active_q <= run_active; end / end / pgood_gen u_pgood_gen ( .clk(clk), / .rst_n(rst_n), / .pwm_sync(Osc_sync), / .pgood_comp(PGOOD_comp_sync), / .run_active(run_active_q),
AIM.237.reason: When the supervisor leaves S_RUN on a trip, UVLO, OTP or disable, PGOOD and switch_supply drop one clock after En instead of on the same clock. This breaks the immediate hand-back the header requires.

AIM.238.description: The CS_n glitch filter is given half the SPI filter length, as if chip select only had to beat the first SCK edge, against the header's rule that all three SPI filters carry identical parameters
AIM.238.reason: A 4-7 clock low glitch on CS_n now selects the slave and is judged as an aborted transaction. A CS rise that closely follows the last SCK edge is also seen before that filtered edge, which cuts the transaction short.

AIM.239.description: The per-strike doubling meant for the hiccup cool-down is also applied to soft_start's ramp rate, so each strike doubles the switching cycles held at every ceiling step of the retry ramp
AIM.239.reason: The first ramp after reset is unchanged (strike_level 0). On a soft-start retry after a hiccup, the ceiling rises half as fast at strike 1 and a quarter as fast at strike 2. PWM_out pulses stay truncated for longer, and SS_done, the S_RUN entry, PGOOD, switch_supply and Green_LED all come later.
